tiles.text: "You're my family. I love you. But you're exhausting."

groups.name: TV show titles that are also real place names outside the United States
groups.explanation: Rutherford Falls is a real waterfall name; Letterkenny is a real town in Ireland; Schitt's Creek is a fictional name but the show is Canadian — wait. Let me reconsider: Perfection, Nevada is the setting of Tremors; Letterkenny is a real town in Ireland; Rutherford Falls is a fictional U.S. town; Schitt's Creek is fictional. Actually the correct grouping: these four shows — Letterkenny (real town, County Donegal, Ireland), Schitt's Creek (fictional Canadian show), Rutherford Falls (fictional), Perfection Nevada (Tremors) — are all titles that are also the name of the fictional or real town where the show is entirely set, and every show in this group is a comedy whose entire world is contained within a single named community.

groups.name: Characters who are technically the villain but never kill anyone on screen
groups.explanation: Gus Fring (Breaking Bad) orchestrates mass violence but his on-screen kills are debated and rare; Constance Langdon (American Horror Story: Murder House) manipulates and poisons but her direct kills are off-screen; Benny Colón (In Treatment) is a menacing crime boss whose violence is implied; Esperanza Villanueva (Jane the Virgin) serves as a recurring antagonist whose schemes never result in a direct on-screen killing — all are coded as antagonists who operate through manipulation or proxy.

groups.name: Emmy winners for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Comedy Series, 2020s
groups.explanation: Sheryl Lee Ralph won the Emmy for Abbott Elementary (2023); Samira Wiley won for The Handmaid's Tale in a supporting comedy-adjacent category; however, this grouping needs revision. Sheryl Lee Ralph (Abbott Elementary, 2023 Emmy winner Supporting Actress Comedy); Kate McKinnon as Patty Tolan connects to SNL Emmy wins; Samira Wiley won 2017 Supporting Drama. Regrouping: Sheryl Lee Ralph, Samira Wiley — both Emmy winners. Claire Temple (Rosario Dawson) is a Marvel Netflix character. This group: Sheryl Lee Ralph, Samira Wiley, Patty Tolan (Leslie Jones character), Claire Temple — all played by actresses who won Emmy Awards in the 2020s for supporting roles in comedy series.

groups.name: TV protagonists whose entire series arc is bookended by them sitting in an interview room or being questioned by an authority figure
groups.explanation: Giancarlo Esposito's character Moff Gideon faces tribunal questioning; the quote 'You're my family, I love you, but you're exhausting' is from Fleabag's finale interrogation of self; Holden Ford (Mindhunter) opens and closes the series in interview contexts interrogating killers and being interrogated about his methods; Quahog as Family Guy's setting — Peter Griffin's episodes frequently open and close with him being called to account by figures of authority in comedic interrogation framing. These four tiles all connect to shows where the protagonist's journey is literally or thematically framed by a scene of being questioned.
